note: A live end-to-end build: the requirements panel, then every build stage, on real models. All text was written by models.
brief: Flag duplicate claims in a batch so a specialist can review them. Two claims are duplicates when they look the same.
facts: A claim has claimId, patientRef (a made-up code), serviceDate, procedureCode and amount. All data is made up.

route.text:
How risky is this change?  → medium · 0.76  (low 0.05 · medium 0.76 · high 0.19)
Does it touch personal, health or financial data?  → yes · 0.59
Can one model handle it safely on its own?  → no · 0.61
Decision: the full panel. Two independent models check each other, and a person signs off at every gate.
A low-risk request, such as fixing a typo, would go to one model and a person, at a fraction of the cost.

panel.draftA:
REQ-1: Within a single batch, the system compares every claim with every other claim on patientRef, serviceDate, procedureCode and amount. claimId is excluded because it identifies each claim. Claims in different batches are not compared. Assumption: "look the same" means all four fields match exactly; the visitor needs to confirm this.
REQ-2: Claims whose four fields all match form one duplicate group. Every claim in the group is flagged. No claim is deleted, edited or rejected automatically; the specialist decides.
REQ-3: The specialist's review list shows each duplicate group with its claimIds and the four matched values. Claims that belong to no group are not flagged and do not appear.
REQ-4: Open question: should near-matches count, such as amounts a few cents apart or service dates one day apart? Until this is confirmed, only exact matches are flagged.
AC-1: The brief gives no sample values, so these examples are invented. Batch: C-1 (patientRef P-001, 2024-03-05, procedureCode 99213, amount 120.00) and C-2 (P-001, 2024-03-05, 99213, 120.00). Result: C-1 and C-2 are flagged as one group.
AC-2: Batch: C-3 (P-002, 2024-03-05, 99213, 120.00) and C-4 (P-002, 2024-03-05, 99213, 125.00). The amounts differ, so neither claim is flagged.
AC-3: Batch: C-5, C-6 and C-7, all with P-003, 2024-03-06, 99214, 80.00. Result: one group of three claims, not three pairs.
AC-4: C-8 (P-004, 2024-03-07, 99213, 120.00) is in batch A and C-9 has identical values but is in batch B. Neither claim is flagged.
panel.draftB:
REQ-1: Read a batch of claims. Each claim has claimId, patientRef, serviceDate, procedureCode and amount. patientRef is a made-up code. All data is made up.
REQ-2: Two claims are duplicates when they look the same. Use no other duplicate rule.
REQ-3: Flag the duplicate claims in that batch so a specialist can review them.
AC-1: Made-up exact match, because the brief has no sample values: claimId 1, patientRef REF1, serviceDate 2024-06-01, procedureCode PC100, amount 100, and a second claim with those same five values. They look the same, so flag both for review.
AC-2: Made-up non-match: the first claim in AC-1 and a claim with claimId 2, patientRef REF1, serviceDate 2024-06-01, procedureCode PC100, amount 80. amount 80 is not amount 100, so they do not look the same and are not flagged.

reviewOfA.strengths: The draft limits comparison to one batch, excludes claimId, treats exact matches on the four shared fields as a confirmed-pending rule, and leaves accept or reject to the specialist, with examples that match those rules.

findings.title: Duplicate criterion left undefined
findings.detail: The brief's phrase 'look the same' is copied without defining which fields must match or how closely. The requirement cannot be built or tested consistently. Record this as an open question for the visitor rather than restating it as a requirement.
findings.quote: REQ-2: Two claims are duplicates when they look the same. Use no other duplicate rule.

findings.title: AC-1 silently invents exact-match rule
findings.detail: AC-1 treats 'look the same' as all five fields being identical, including claimId. That is a second rule, which REQ-2 forbids. It also means resubmitted claims with new claimIds would never be flagged. State the assumption explicitly or ask the visitor.
findings.quote: a second claim with those same five values. They look the same, so flag both for review.

findings.title: AC-2 changes two fields
findings.detail: The non-match claim differs in claimId (2 vs 1) as well as amount, yet only amount is named as the reason. Varying a single field would make the test show clearly which difference prevents the flag.
findings.quote: amount 80 is not amount 100, so they do not look the same and are not flagged.

reviewOfB.strengths: The draft uses only the given fields, labels every sample value as made up, and keeps the scope to a single batch as the brief asks.

merge.document:
REQ-1: The system reads one batch of claims. Each claim has claimId, patientRef (a made-up code), serviceDate, procedureCode and amount. All data is made up.
REQ-2: Within a single batch, the system compares every claim with every other claim on patientRef, serviceDate, procedureCode and amount. claimId is excluded because it identifies each claim, so a resubmitted claim with a new claimId can still be flagged. Claims in different batches are not compared. Assumption: 'look the same' means all four fields match exactly. The visitor needs to confirm this.
REQ-3: Claims whose four fields all match form one duplicate group. Every claim in the group is flagged. No claim is deleted, edited or rejected automatically; the specialist decides.
REQ-4: The specialist's review list shows each duplicate group with its claimIds and the four matched values. Claims that belong to no group are not flagged and do not appear.
REQ-5: Open question for the visitor: should near-matches count, such as amounts a few cents apart or service dates one day apart? Until this is confirmed, only exact matches are flagged.
AC-1: The brief gives no sample values, so these examples are invented. Batch: C-1 (patientRef P-001, 2024-03-05, procedureCode 99213, amount 120.00) and C-2 (P-001, 2024-03-05, 99213, 120.00). Result: C-1 and C-2 are flagged as one group, even though their claimIds differ.
AC-2: Batch: C-3 (P-002, 2024-03-05, 99213, 120.00) and C-4 (P-002, 2024-03-05, 99213, 125.00). Only amount differs among the compared fields, so neither claim is flagged.
AC-3: Batch: C-5, C-6 and C-7, all with P-003, 2024-03-06, 99214, 80.00. Result: one group of three claims, not three pairs.
AC-4: C-8 (P-004, 2024-03-07, 99213, 120.00) is in batch A, and C-9 has identical values but is in batch B. Neither claim is flagged.
merge.keptFromA: I kept draft A's whole structure: four compared fields with claimId excluded, comparison within one batch, the stated assumption and open question on near-matches, group flagging with no automatic action, and its four acceptance examples.
merge.keptFromB: I kept draft B's opening requirement that lists the claim fields and states that patientRef and all data are made up.

resolutions.note: REQ-2 defines 'look the same' as an exact match on patientRef, serviceDate, procedureCode and amount, and labels this as an assumption the visitor must confirm. REQ-5 records near-matches as an open question.

resolutions.finding: D-B2 · AC-1 silently invents exact-match rule
resolutions.note: The exact-match rule is now stated as an explicit assumption. claimId is excluded from the comparison, and AC-1 shows that two claims with different claimIds are still flagged, so resubmitted claims are caught.
AC-2 now differs only in amount among the compared fields. claimId is not compared, so its difference does not affect the result.

finalReview.strengths: The draft stays within the given fields, flags only same-batch exact matches for a specialist to review, and every example amount, date, and grouping result checks out.

build.contract: findDuplicateGroups(claims) where claims is an array holding one batch of claim objects, each { claimId: string, patientRef: string (a made-up code such as "P-001"), serviceDate: string (YYYY-MM-DD, such as "2024-03-05"), procedureCode: string (such as "99213"), amount: number (such as 120.00) }. Returns { groups: Array<{ claimIds: string[] (the claimIds in the group, at least two), patientRef: string, serviceDate: string, procedureCode: string, amount: number (the four matched values) }> }, with groups empty when nothing is flagged. Throws an Error whose message is "unknown field: <name>" if any claim has any other field. Each call takes exactly one batch, so claims in different batches are passed in separate calls.

architecture.draft:
Components: one pure function findDuplicateGroups(claims) in a single module, with no I/O, storage or UI. The review list is built from its return value, and nothing is deleted, edited or rejected.
Validation: for each claim, any key other than claimId, patientRef, serviceDate, procedureCode or amount throws Error("unknown field: <name>"), naming the first such key found.
Keying: the match key is JSON.stringify([patientRef, serviceDate, procedureCode, amount]). claimId is excluded, matching is exact only, and JSON avoids delimiter collisions. The amount stays a number, so 120 and 120.00 match while 120.00 and 125.00 do not (AC-2).
Data: a Map from match key to { claimIds, the four values } in insertion order. Each claim is appended to its key's entry in one pass, which is O(n) rather than pairwise.
Output: keep only entries with 2 or more claimIds and return { groups }. Groups and claimIds follow first appearance in the input, and groups is empty if nothing matches. AC-3 yields one group [C-5, C-6, C-7].
Batch scope: each call holds exactly one batch, so cross-batch claims are never compared (AC-4).
Tests: AC-1 to AC-4, plus the unknown-field error, an empty batch and a single-claim batch.
File fence (only these may change): src/claims/findDuplicateGroups.js and test/claims/findDuplicateGroups.test.js.
Open for the visitor (REQ-5): near-matches stay out of scope. Contract gap: the contract does not say what happens when a field is missing or has the wrong type, so the code makes no assumption until this is decided.
architecture.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: Exact grouping on the four fields, with claimId excluded, yields one group per match set, omits non-duplicates, stays inside a single batch, and does not delete, edit, or reject claims.
architecture.final:
Components: one pure function findDuplicateGroups(claims) in a single module, with no I/O, storage or UI. The review list is built from its return value, and nothing is deleted, edited or rejected.
Validation: for each claim, any key other than claimId, patientRef, serviceDate, procedureCode or amount throws Error("unknown field: <name>"), naming the first such key found.
Keying: the match key is JSON.stringify([patientRef, serviceDate, procedureCode, amount]). claimId is excluded, matching is exact only, and JSON avoids delimiter collisions. The amount stays a number, so 120 and 120.00 match, while 120.00 and 125.00 do not (AC-2).
Data: a Map from match key to { claimIds, the four values }, kept in insertion order. Each claim is appended to its key's entry in one pass. This is O(n) rather than pairwise.
Output: keep only entries with 2 or more claimIds and return { groups }. Groups and claimIds follow first appearance in the input, and groups is empty if nothing matches. AC-3 yields one group [C-5, C-6, C-7].
Batch scope: each call holds exactly one batch, so cross-batch claims are never compared (AC-4).
Tests: AC-1 to AC-4, plus the unknown-field error, an empty batch and a single-claim batch.
File fence (only these may change): src/claims/findDuplicateGroups.js and test/claims/findDuplicateGroups.test.js.
Open for the visitor (REQ-5): near-matches stay out of scope.
Contract gap: the contract does not say what happens when a field is missing or has the wrong type. The code adds no checks for these cases, so the behavior is unspecified until this is decided (JSON.stringify turns a missing value into null).

code.summary: This is one expression that returns { findDuplicateGroups }. It first checks every claim and throws Error("unknown field: <name>") for the first key that is not one of the five allowed fields. That check runs before any grouping. Each claim's match key is JSON.stringify([patientRef, serviceDate, procedureCode, amount]). The key leaves out claimId and uses exact matching only. Amount stays a number, so 120 and 120.00 match but 120.00 and 125.00 do not. A Map in insertion order collects claimIds for each key in a single O(n) pass. Only entries with 2 or more claimIds are returned, in order of first appearance. The result is { groups }, which is empty when nothing matches. Each call covers one batch, so claims in different batches are never compared. Nothing is deleted, edited or rejected. Checked against the PRD: AC-1 gives [C-1, C-2]. AC-2 gives no groups because the amounts differ. AC-3 gives one group [C-5, C-6, C-7]. AC-4 gives no groups because the two claims come in separate calls. The module does not validate missing fields or wrong types, because the contract does not cover them. A missing value is encoded as null in the key, as the architecture records. Near-matches (REQ-5) stay out of scope until the visitor confirms.
code.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: Exact four-field grouping excludes claimId, returns only groups of at least two, throws the required unknown-field error, and keeps no state across calls so separate batches are not compared.
code.resolutions: No defects found; strengths: exact four-field grouping excluding claimId, only groups of two or more returned, required unknown-field error thrown, no state kept across calls. applied: I agree after checking the code myself, so the module is returned unchanged. AC-1: C-1 and C-2 share a key and form one group. AC-2: the amounts 120 and 125 give different keys, so nothing is flagged. AC-3: C-5, C-6 and C-7 form one group of three. AC-4: separate calls share no state, so nothing is flagged. Numeric 120.00 and 120 are equal, and string values cannot collide with numbers in the JSON key. Open item from REQ-2 and REQ-5: the visitor still needs to confirm that only exact matches count as duplicates.

testCases: TC-1 · REQ-2, REQ-3, REQ-4 exact match ignores claimId · one batch: C-1 (P-001, 2024-03-05, 99213, 120.00), C-2 (P-001, 2024-03-05, 99213, 120.00) → one group flagged with claimIds C-1 and C-2 and matched values P-001, 2024-03-05, 99213, 120.00
TC-2 · REQ-2 all four fields must match exactly · one batch: C-3 (P-002, 2024-03-05, 99213, 120.00), C-4 (P-002, 2024-03-05, 99213, 125.00) → no group; neither claim flagged
TC-3 · REQ-3 one group not pairs · one batch: C-5, C-6, C-7 all (P-003, 2024-03-06, 99214, 80.00) → one group of three claimIds C-5, C-6, C-7, not three pairs
TC-4 · REQ-1, REQ-2 compare only within one batch · batch A: C-8 (P-004, 2024-03-07, 99213, 120.00); batch B: C-9 (P-004, 2024-03-07, 99213, 120.00) → neither claim flagged

TC-5 · REQ-4 ungrouped claims omitted · one batch: C-1 and C-2 as in TC-1, plus C-10 (P-010, 2024-04-01, 99215, 50.00) → review list shows only the C-1/C-2 group with those four matched values; C-10 is not flagged and does not appear

TC-6 · REQ-5 near-matches not flagged until confirmed · one batch: C-11 (P-005, 2024-03-08, 99213, 120.00), C-12 (P-005, 2024-03-08, 99213, 120.03), C-13 (P-006, 2024-03-08, 99213, 90.00), C-14 (P-006, 2024-03-09, 99213, 90.00) → no groups; cents-apart amounts and one-day-apart dates are not flagged

TC-8 · REQ-3, REQ-4 separate groups · one batch: C-15 and C-16 both (P-007, 2024-03-10, 99213, 40.00); C-17 and C-18 both (P-008, 2024-03-11, 99214, 60.00) → two groups, each with its own claimIds and its own four matched values

diagram.summary: A batch of claims flows into the new pure function findDuplicateGroups, which rejects unknown fields, groups claims in an in-memory map by an exact key of patientRef, serviceDate, procedureCode and amount, and returns groups of two or more claim IDs from which the specialist's review list is built, with nothing deleted, edited or rejected.
